questions.q: What is the World of Measurement?
a: A mindset where survival feels hard and resources seem limited
A society that judges people by their income and status
A scientific approach to solving everyday problems
A habit of planning every hour of the day
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes the World of Measurement as a place of survival and scarcity, opposed to possibility.

questions.q: What does the summary say blocks us from living in possibility?
a: Our own assumptions, which shape how we see reality
A lack of money and useful connections
Other people's unwillingness to help
Not having enough information about the world
questions.why: Lesson 1 says our assumptions filter reality and that getting past them opens the door to possibility.

questions.q: According to the summary, where does happiness come from?
a: Helping others rather than being successful
Achieving goals and earning recognition
Having more freedom than other people
Removing all failure from your life
questions.why: Lesson 2 states that happiness arises from helping others, not from success.

questions.q: In the rainy holiday example, what two options does the summary describe?
a: Mourn the trip you imagined or enjoy the trip as it actually is
Demand a refund or stay in the hotel room
Change destinations or cut the trip short
Pretend the weather is fine or complain to your partner
questions.why: Lesson 3 uses the rained-out holiday to show the choice between resenting reality and making the best of it.

questions.q: What does the summary recommend doing with difficult feelings?
a: Face them and feel them fully rather than trying to escape
Distract yourself until they pass on their own
Explain them away with positive thinking
Save them for a therapy session later
questions.why: Lesson 3 advises facing uncomfortable feelings completely instead of hiding from the storm.
